title: Nightly quant bisect notes — NaN regression hunt
content:
Context and goal:
- Nightly synthesis runner started failing intermittently with NaNs in downstream logits for customer workload samples (mostly long-context chat).
- Goal: bisect commit range, identify code path/regression, capture minimal repro and candidate fix ideas.

High-level observations (summary):
- Failure mode: NaN shows up in final logits at token generation time (post-softmax logit vector contains +Inf/NaN), causing streaming to abort.
- Frequency: ~1/14 runs on nightly CI for the same input; easier to reproduce when sequence length > 1024 and when prefix caching is enabled.
- Affected quant modes: reproduces with int8 quantized weights and fp8 fast-path enabled. BF16-only runs do NOT show NaNs.
- Suspect area: quantized matmul / kv-cache write path when streaming + partial KV cache flush.

Environment & reproducible runner details:
- Docker image: redwood/runtime-nightly:2025-02-01-23-utc (contains commit range commit A..commit B)
- Sample input: examples/nightly/long-chat-1.json (attached to runner)
- Hardware used: G5.12xlarge (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) and local dev with A100 repro.
- Repro harness (simplified):
  git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/serving-runtime.git && cd serving-runtime
  git checkout <bisected-commit>
  ./tools/run_local_repro.sh --model quantized/ggml-int8-fp8-backend --input examples/nightly/long-chat-1.json --stream --cache-prefix on

Commands run during bisect:
- Standard bisect:
  git bisect start HEAD -- good-tag
  git bisect run ./tools/nightly_bisect_script.sh || true

- Manual repro run (capture logs):
  ./tools/run_local_repro.sh --model quantized/ggml-int8-fp8-backend --input examples/nightly/long-chat-1.json --seed 20250202 --capture-activations /tmp/act-dump --log-level debug > /tmp/repro.log 2>&1

Key error snippets (from /tmp/repro.log):
- C++ runtime error near token 127:
  [2025-02-07 03:12:14.892] ERROR runtime::kv_cache: write failed: NaN encountered in KV write buffer
- Upstream math kernel warning:
  [flash_mm] WARN: detected large scale (>1e4) in int8 dequant path, clamping to avoid overflow
- Final collapse (Python harness):
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/opt/runtime/generation.py", line 438, in stream_step
      out = model.step(ctx)
    File "/opt/runtime/model_wrapper.py", line 221, in step
      logits = backend.compute_logits(last_token_ids)
  RuntimeError: NaN in logits (index=3, value=nan)

Activation dumps & quick stats (from /tmp/act-dump):
- LayerNorm pre-normalization mean/std per layer (layers 6..12): means in [-2.1, 3.6], std in [0.85, 1.9]. No obvious exploding value pre-LN.
- After matmul (QK and attention output), see single extremely large value at layer 9 matmul output: 6.1e38 (float32), then subsequent micro-kernel writes cause +/-Inf in int8 dequant path.
- KV buffer snapshot: contains 0x7F... pattern at write offset -> indicates memory got NaN/Inf encoded into quantized buffer.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Per-channel scale mismatch between quantization and dequantization for certain layers (e.g., row-scale computed with cached min/max stale when streaming), leading to dequant overflow -> NaN.
2) FP8 kernel exponent clamp bug: when intermediate exponent underflow/overflow occurs, some code path returns huge value instead of properly clamping to +/-max. This interacts badly with int8 dequant later.
3) KV cache write race: when cache flush happens concurrently with write, partially-initialized cache pages are processed by quant kernels leading to garbage being interpreted as floats. Race shows up intermittently -> explains non-determinism.
4) Incorrect fallback logic: code attempts to fallback from fp8 fast-path to bf16 but leaves scale arrays (per-channel) populated with garbage, used later by dequant.

Repro tests and what they showed:
- Forcing no-prefix-cache (./run_local_repro.sh --cache-prefix off) reduces frequency to 0/20 -> supports KV-cache involvement.
- Running with --deterministic-kernels (disables some async tiling) makes failure deterministic at commit XYZ -> points to concurrency scheduling.
- Replacing fp8 path with bf16 (env USE_FP8=0) prevents NaNs -> supports hypothesis #2/#4.
- Instrumented per-layer scale recompute (force recompute every token) also prevents failure -> supports hypothesis #1.

Minimal repro script (local) used for quick experiments:
- tools/min_repro.sh (excerpt):
  #!/bin/bash
  export RUNTIME_DEBUG=1
  export USE_FP8=1
  ./bin/rv_runtime --model $1 --input $2 --stream --cache-prefix $3 --dump-activations /tmp/a

Notes from native kernel debug (Marco):
- Found a spot in quant_dequant.cc where per-channel scales are lazily updated. If a concurrent write clears the shadow buffer, the scale ptr can be zero-length while code still reads old index. Added assert catches this but test harness didn't trigger it until commit 2025-01-31.
- In fp8_fastpath.cu we use __half2float magic for fast path and an inline clamp that uses bit-twiddling; one code branch returns huge value on underflow for certain compiler flags (GCC 12 vs 11 difference).

Candidate quick mitigations tried (results):
- Add atomic guard around KV cache write: reduces frequency but not 100% reliable on CI. (temp patch in branch fix/atomic-kv-guard)
- Always recompute per-channel scales at first token after cache flush: prevented failure locally but added ~4% latency cost.
- Force bf16 fallback when prefix cache enabled: removes failure but changes numerical profile (could impact customer quality).

Next steps / planned experiments (ordered):
1) Reproduce deterministic failure by combining: --cache-prefix on, --deterministic-kernels on, USE_FP8=1. Get exact commit that failed with git bisect result: good=commit@2025-01-18, bad=commit@2025-02-01 -> commit 2025-01-28b introduced lazy-scale write.
2) Add targeted unit test that simulates concurrent KV write + kernel dequant reads (C++ test harness). Try to get ASAN/TSAN to flag races.
3) Instrument per-channel-scale lifetime (refcounts) and add sanity asserts in debug builds; run nightly with debug image for 48h to catch flakiness.
4) Prepare two candidate PRs: (A) immediate safe-fallback: recompute scales and add atomic guard (low risk, perf cost); (B) long-term: fix lazy-scale lifecycle and kernel clamp behavior (higher effort). Run canary on dedicated infra.

Open questions / things I couldn't yet verify:
- Is the fp8 exponent clamp returning NaN upstream or is dequant overflow turning large floats into NaN? Need to add checkpoints after each kernel to distinguish.
- Are certain model architectures more susceptible (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder)? So far we see decoder-only (chat models) primarily.
- Is there a correlation with batch size >1? Preliminary tests show single-batch fails more often (weirder).

Quick notes for the next person who picks this up:
- Check out branch fix/atomic-kv-guard for experimental guard code and compare reproduction frequency.
- Use the repro harness flags: --seed 20250202 --dump-activations /tmp/act-dump --capture-kv-metadata to gather exact offsets.
- If you have access to A100 devbox, reproduce there (I saw same failure on A100 + H100).

References / links in case helpful:
- tools/run_local_repro.sh (internal script)
- tools/nightly_bisect_script.sh (used with git bisect)
- Candidate PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2389 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2391

Short-term decision needed (proposal): merge low-risk recompute-scales + atomic guard to trunk to stop customer-facing NaNs, schedule the kernel clamp/fp8 fix for next sprint.

Log tail (example failing run):
[2025-02-07 03:12:14.891] INFO kernel: running attention_kv_write layer=9 token=126
[2025-02-07 03:12:14.892] ERROR runtime::kv_cache: write failed: NaN encountered in KV write buffer (offset=0x1f400)
[2025-02-07 03:12:14.892] WARN flash_mm: possible overflow in int8 dequant (scale=1.2e+05)
[2025-02-07 03:12:14.893] INFO runtime: falling back to bf16-path for subsequent tokens
[2025-02-07 03:12:14.897] ERROR runtime: generation aborted: NaN in logits

-- Aisha
